title: Metaphor
about: Metaphorical collocations: words for light and dark, water, and fire and heat that describe feelings, crowds and arguments, like a sunny smile, floods of tears and a heated discussion.

parts.title: Tip
parts.note: Помічай метафори, коли читаєш англійською. Знайомі слова про світло, воду й вогонь часто описують почуття, людей і суперечки. Такі сполучення частіше трапляються в письмовій мові й звучать трохи поетично. Ось ще кілька образів, які легко знайти у словнику: bright — розумний або успішний, warm — дружній, cold — недружній.

rows: a future that looks happy and successful
With her talent for music, she has a bright future.
a clever child who learns quickly
He's a bright child. He could read before he was four.
The hotel staff gave us a warm welcome after our long journey.
The nurse gave the nervous little boy a warm smile.
The security guard looked at us with cold eyes.
When I asked for tap water, the waiter gave me a cold stare.

items.pattern: a sunny smile · a sunny face / nature
items.meaning: a happy, cheerful smile that makes people feel good, like sunshine
items.example: The little girl next door always waves at us with a **sunny smile**.
more: The children came out of school with **sunny faces**: the holidays had started.
My aunt has a **sunny nature**, and nothing upsets her for long.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий, що в українській: сонячна усмішка — a sunny smile. Але не solar: solar — лише технічне слово (solar panels, solar energy).

items.pattern: sb's eyes / face shine with excitement / pleasure / delight · shine – shone – shone
items.meaning: someone's eyes or face look bright because they feel very happy or excited
items.example: When the fireworks started, the children's eyes **shone with excitement**.
more: Her face **shone with pleasure** when she opened the letter from the university.
My daughter's eyes **shine with delight** every time she sees a horse.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий — сяяти від радості, але прийменник інший: shine with excitement, не from. Минулий час — shone, британською вимовляється /ʃɒn/.

items.pattern: sb's face / eyes light up · light – lit – lit
items.meaning: someone suddenly looks very happy or interested
items.example: Tom's face **lit up** when he saw his old friend at the station.
more: My son's eyes **light up** every time we walk past the toy shop.
Her whole face **lit up** when the waiter brought out the birthday cake.
items.watchOut: Українською очі «загоряються» (образ вогню), англійською — засвічуються (образ світла): his eyes lit up, а не burned чи caught fire. Минулий час — lit up.

items.pattern: the mood / atmosphere lightens · lighten the mood / atmosphere
items.meaning: a situation becomes more relaxed and cheerful, less tense or serious
items.example: When Dad started telling silly jokes, the **atmosphere lightened** at once.
more: The **mood lightened** once the sun came out and the picnic could finally start.
A bit of music might **lighten the mood** in here.
items.watchOut: Українською атмосферу «розряджають» (образ електрики), англійською її роблять легшою й світлішою: lighten the atmosphere, не discharge. Не плутай з light up: lighten — стати легшим чи світлішим, light up — засяяти (про обличчя, очі).

items.pattern: dark thoughts · have / push away dark thoughts
items.meaning: sad, gloomy or worrying thoughts
items.example: Going for a long walk helps me get rid of **dark thoughts**.
more: After he lost his job, he was full of **dark thoughts** for weeks.
Talk to someone if **dark thoughts** keep you awake at night.
items.watchOut: Українською думки частіше «чорні», а англійською звичайне сполучення — dark thoughts (black thoughts трапляється рідко й звучить книжно). Black краще знати в іншому сполученні: a black mood — дуже поганий настрій.

items.pattern: dark days / dark times · go through / live through dark days
items.meaning: a difficult, unhappy period in someone's life or in history
items.example: Our family went through some **dark days** when Mum was ill, but we never gave up.
more: Friends who stay with you in **dark times** are the ones that matter.
Those first weeks in a new country were **dark days** for me: no job, no friends and no money.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий: темні часи — dark times, dark days. Але «відкласти на чорний день» англійською — save for a rainy day (інший образ: дощ, а не темрява).

items.pattern: sb's face / eyes / expression darkens
items.meaning: someone suddenly looks angry, worried or unhappy
items.example: My boss's face **darkened** when I told him the order would be late.
more: Her **expression darkened** as she read the electricity bill.
His **eyes darkened** when his brother laughed at him in front of everyone.
items.watchOut: Образ схожий: спохмурніти, потемніти на лиці. Кажуть his face darkened, не became dark. Darken — частіше про гнів або тривогу; якщо людина просто розчарувалася, кажуть his face fell.

items.pattern: the ideas / the conversation flow(s) · flow easily / freely
items.meaning: ideas come easily, or people talk easily without awkward pauses
items.uk: ідеї так і сиплються; розмова ллється
items.example: We sat in the garden with a big pot of tea, and the **conversation flowed** until midnight.
more: With old friends, the **conversation** always **flows**, even after years apart.
A walk in the park helps me think, and the **ideas** really **flow**.
items.watchOut: Розмова «ллється» — той самий образ води: the conversation flowed. А ідеї українською «сиплються» (як зерно), англійською — течуть: the ideas flowed.

items.pattern: be in floods of tears · burst into a flood of tears
items.meaning: crying a lot, often for a long time
items.example: My little sister was **in floods of tears** when her goldfish died.
more: She was **in floods of tears** after the phone call, so I made her a cup of tea.
When she finally saw her son at arrivals, she burst into **a flood of tears**.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий — сльози заливають, як повінь. Після be форма стала: be in floods of tears (з in і в множині), не with floods of tears. В однині кажуть burst into a flood of tears.

items.pattern: tears stream / are streaming down sb's face / cheeks
items.meaning: a lot of tears run down someone's face without stopping
items.example: The onions were so strong that **tears were streaming down my face**.
more: She read the last page of the novel with **tears streaming down her face**.
**Tears streamed down his face** as his team lifted the cup.
items.watchOut: Українською сльози «котяться» або «течуть», і англійською так теж можна (tears rolled / ran down her cheeks). Stream додає, що сліз дуже багато і вони не зупиняються, як струмок.

items.pattern: people pour / stream out of / into / through a place
items.meaning: a lot of people move in one direction quickly and continuously
items.example: When the rain stopped, people **poured out** of the shops onto the high street.
more: Fans were **streaming into** the stadium two hours before kick-off.
As soon as the gates opened, families **poured into** the zoo.
items.watchOut: Українською люди «висипають» на вулицю або «валять» натовпом, англійською — ллються, як вода: people poured out. Не fell out: fall out with sb — посваритися.

items.pattern: people / cars trickle in / out / back · a trickle of people / cars
items.meaning: a few people or cars come or go slowly, in small numbers
items.example: The film started at eight, but people kept **trickling in** for the first twenty minutes.
more: By nine o'clock, only a few guests had **trickled in**.
There was only **a trickle of** people on the beach because of the wind.
items.watchOut: Українською люди «підтягуються» чи «сходяться потроху», без образу води. Англійською — trickle (текти цівкою): people trickled in. Протилежне — pour: люди йдуть натовпом.

items.pattern: a (steady / constant) stream of traffic / visitors / customers
items.meaning: a lot of cars or people, one after another, without a break
items.example: We couldn't cross the road because of the endless **stream of traffic**.
more: The new bakery has had a steady **stream of customers** since it opened.
All weekend there was a **stream of visitors** at the door, bringing flowers and cards.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий: потік машин — a stream of traffic (можна й a flow of traffic). Але не current: current — це течія в річці або електричний струм.

items.pattern: a heated discussion / debate / conversation / argument
items.meaning: a discussion in which people disagree strongly and get angry or excited
items.example: We had a **heated discussion** about whose turn it was to do the washing-up.
more: There's always a **heated debate** in our house about where to go on holiday.
My parents had a **heated conversation** in the kitchen, but by dinner they were laughing again.
items.watchOut: Українська теж бере образ жару (гаряча дискусія), але англійською — heated, не hot: a heated discussion. Hot discussion так не кажуть.

items.pattern: have / have got a fiery temper
items.meaning: a tendency to get angry quickly and strongly
items.example: My grandfather had a **fiery temper**, but he never stayed angry for long.
more: Our football coach has a **fiery temper**, so nobody is ever late for training.
She's lovely most of the time, but she has a **fiery temper** when she's tired.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий — вогонь (запальний). Але «характер» тут — temper, не character: a fiery temper. Можна й a hot temper або a quick temper. Пишеться fiery, не firey.

items.pattern: tempers flare / flared · sb's temper flares
items.meaning: people suddenly become angry with each other
items.example: It was a long, hot day at the airport, and **tempers flared** in the queue.
more: **Tempers** often **flare** at family dinners when politics comes up.
Her **temper flared** when the bus drove past without stopping.
items.watchOut: Українською теж вогонь: пристрасті розпалилися, сварка спалахнула. Але англійською спалахує temper (гнів), не nerves і не characters: tempers flared.

items.pattern: violence / trouble / fighting flares up · an old injury flares up
items.meaning: a problem that had calmed down suddenly becomes serious again
items.example: Police were called when **trouble flared up** outside the pub after the match.
more: **Violence flared up** again in the area after a week of calm.
My old knee injury **flared up** after the long walk.
items.watchOut: Про насильство образ той самий: спалахнути — flare up. А про хворобу українською кажуть «загострилася», англійською теж вогонь: my back has flared up again.

items.pattern: sb's cheeks / face burn(s) with embarrassment · burned / burnt
items.meaning: someone's face goes hot and red because they feel embarrassed
items.example: When I realised I'd called my teacher 'Mum', my **cheeks burned with embarrassment**.
more: Her **face burned with embarrassment** when her phone rang during the concert.
I could feel my **cheeks burning** as everyone turned to look at me.
items.watchOut: Образ той самий: щоки горять. Прийменник — with: burn with embarrassment (як shine with joy). «Сором» тут — embarrassment, ніяковість; shame — глибший, моральний сором.

items.pattern: in / amid a blaze of publicity
items.meaning: a lot of attention from newspapers, TV and the internet
items.example: The new shopping centre opened in **a blaze of publicity**, with TV cameras everywhere.
more: The singer's wedding took place in **a blaze of publicity**.
The book came out in **a blaze of publicity**, but hardly anyone read it.
items.watchOut: Українською про таку увагу кажуть «гучний розголос» (образ звуку) або «шквал публікацій» (образ вітру). Англійською — яскраве полум'я: a blaze of publicity.

items.pattern: (go out / finish / retire) in a blaze of glory
items.meaning: in a very impressive, exciting way that everyone notices, often at the end of something
items.example: Our village team finished the season in **a blaze of glory**, winning their last six games.
more: The old cinema closed **in a blaze of glory** with a free film festival.
He wanted to retire **in a blaze of glory**, not just quietly disappear.
items.watchOut: Українською слава «сяє» або це «вершина слави», англійською — яскраве полум'я: in a blaze of glory. Найчастіше так кажуть про гучний кінець: go out in a blaze of glory.

warmup.uk: У нової вчительки така сонячна усмішка!
warmup.q: The new teacher has such a ___ smile!
warmup.explain: Сонячна усмішка — a sunny smile. Solar — лише технічне: solar panels.

warmup.uk: Його очі загорілися, коли він побачив новий велосипед.
warmup.q: His eyes ___ when he saw the new bike.
warmup.explain: Очі «загоряються» — англійською lit up: образ світла, а не вогню.

warmup.uk: Тато розповів анекдот, щоб розрядити атмосферу.
warmup.q: Dad told a joke to ___ the atmosphere.
warmup.explain: Розрядити атмосферу — lighten the atmosphere (або lighten the mood).

warmup.uk: Коли я прийшла, сестра заливалася сльозами.
warmup.q: When I arrived, my sister was in ___ of tears.
warmup.explain: Заливатися сльозами — be in floods of tears: з in і в множині.

warmup.uk: Після концерту люди висипали на вулицю.
warmup.q: After the concert, people ___ out onto the street.
warmup.explain: Люди «висипали» натовпом — англійською ллються, як вода: poured out (або streamed out).

warmup.uk: У нас із сусідами була гаряча дискусія про паркування.
warmup.q: We had a ___ discussion with the neighbours about parking.
warmup.explain: Гаряча дискусія — a heated discussion. Hot discussion англійською не кажуть.

warmup.q: By the end of the meeting, ___ had flared.
warmup.explain: Пристрасті розпалилися — tempers flared. Temper — гнів, запальність.

warmup.uk: Коли я переплутав ім'я начальника, мої щоки горіли від сорому.
warmup.q: When I got my boss's name wrong, my cheeks ___ with embarrassment.
warmup.explain: Щоки горять від сорому — cheeks burn with embarrassment, з with.

A.q: Everyone was nervous before the exam, so our teacher told a funny story to ___ the mood.
A.explain: Lighten the mood — розрядити атмосферу. Darken — навпаки, зіпсувати настрій.

A.q: When she heard she'd got her dream job, her face ___.
A.explain: Light up — раптом засяяти від радості. Darken — спохмурніти від гніву чи тривоги.

A.q: He had a lot of ___ thoughts after his business failed.

B.q: The party was a success: the music was good and the conversation ___ all night.
B.explain: The conversation flowed — розмова лилася легко. Trickle — текти цівкою, про небагатьох людей.

B.q: Nobody was in a hurry, so the guests ___ in one or two at a time.
B.explain: Trickle in — приходити потроху, по одному-двоє. Pour і flood — натовпом.

B.q: In August, our seaside town gets a steady ___ of tourists.
B.explain: Потік туристів — a stream of tourists. Current — течія або струм.

C.q: The parents' meeting turned into a ___ discussion about school uniforms.
C.explain: Гаряча дискусія — a heated discussion. Hot і boiling тут не працюють.

C.q: When the shop ran out of bread on Christmas Eve, tempers ___.
C.explain: Tempers flared — люди почали злитися одне на одного.

C.q: Rita has a ___ temper, so don't argue with her.
C.explain: Запальний характер — a fiery temper. Heated кажуть про дискусії та суперечки, а не про temper.

example.title: A wedding to remember
example.uk:
Весілля моєї двоюрідної сестри почалося під яскравим сонцем. Наречена увійшла із сонячною усмішкою, а коли побачила нареченого, усе її обличчя засяяло. Під кінець шлюбних обітниць бабуся вже заливалася сльозами.

За вечерею розмова лилася легко, аж поки дядько Піт і мій тато не почали гарячу суперечку про футбол. У дядька Піта запальний характер, і незабаром пристрасті розпалилися. Обличчя моєї тітки спохмурніло.

Потім заграв гурт, і гості ринули на танцмайданчик. Настрій одразу покращився. Коли наречена потягла мене танцювати, мої щоки горіли від сорому, але я все одно пішов у танок.
example.en:
My cousin's wedding started in bright sunshine. The bride walked in with a [[sunny smile|a1]], and when she saw the groom, her whole face [[lit up|a3]]. By the end of the vows, Grandma was [[in floods of tears|b2]].

At dinner, the [[conversation flowed|b1]] easily, until Uncle Pete and my dad started a [[heated discussion|c1]] about football. Uncle Pete has a [[fiery temper|c2]], and soon [[tempers flared|c3]]. My aunt's [[face darkened|a7]].

Then the band began to play, and the guests [[poured|b4]] onto the dance floor. The [[mood lightened|a4]] at once. When the bride pulled me up to dance, my [[cheeks burned with embarrassment|c5]], but I joined in anyway.
